thread:
raj-customer: Hi team — our Redwood Private agents in prod started failing to register ~10m ago. We see repeated heartbeats and then disconnects. Asking for urgent help, customer impact: background jobs failing.

mike-support: Sorry, looking. Can you paste the agent pod logs (redwood-agent) and the namespace/networkpolicy config? Also which CNI are you running?

raj-customer: We're on weave-net CNI. Logs from the agent below (kubectl logs -n redwood redwood-agent-0):

redwood-agent-bot: [2026-03-14T09:12:11Z] connecting to control-plane.redwood.example.com:443
redwood-agent-bot: [2026-03-14T09:12:21Z] dial tcp 10.20.30.5:443: i/o timeout
redwood-agent-bot: [2026-03-14T09:12:31Z] retrying...

laura-sre: i/o timeout suggests egress to control plane IP is blocked or blackholed. Can you run `kubectl exec -n redwood -it redwood-agent-0 -- curl -v https://control-plane.redwood.example.com:443 --resolve control-plane.redwood.example.com:10.20.30.5` and show output?

raj-customer: paste:
* Trying 10.20.30.5:443...
* connect to 10.20.30.5 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to control-plane.redwood.example.com port 443: Connection timed out

mike-support: From a cluster node (not pod), if you run `curl -v https://10.20.30.5:443 --interface eth0` does it succeed? If node->controlplane works but pod->controlplane doesn't, likely NetworkPolicy or CNI egress ACL.

raj-customer: node->controlplane works fine. Pod->controlplane times out. We have a default-deny egress networkpolicy for the redwood namespace. Here's the NP we applied yesterday (truncated):

---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-external-egress
  namespace: redwood
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
---

laura-sre: ah, empty egress leads to all egress dropped. But you also mentioned intermittent TLS timeouts and some pods could register intermittently?

raj-customer: yes, sometimes they connect for a short time then drop. We also saw strange TLS errors in some logs: `remote error: tls: internal error` and some `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` earlier during rollout.

jess-devex: two things to check: 1) DNS (UDP 53) egress must be allowed for the agent to resolve control-plane endpoint, and 2) ICMP 'fragmentation needed' (Path MTU Discovery) — if ICMP is blocked by firewall it can cause TLS handshake stalls for larger TLS records due to PMTU blackhole. Can you capture from a pod?

raj-customer: ran tcpdump on pod interface (weave) while trying to curl:

13:45:21.123456 IP redwood-agent > 10.20.30.5: Flags [S], seq 0, win 26880, length 0
13:45:21.223789 IP 10.20.30.5 > redwood-agent: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
13:46:10.000001 IP 10.20.30.1 > redwood-agent: ICMP 3/4, \"Fragmentation needed and DF set\"
13:46:10.000123 IP redwood-agent > 10.20.30.5: Flags [P.], seq 1:1377, ack 1, win 65535, length 1376

mike-support: That ICMP 3/4 indicates a PMTU discovery message from an intermediate router telling the pod to reduce MSS. If your firewall or egress ACL is dropping ICMP (or NetworkPolicy blocks it), TCP flow can stall; particularly TLS can fail or time out for larger records.

laura-sre: Also, some CNIs (weave) encapsulate traffic, increasing packet size — PMTU matters. If your egress rules only allow TCP/443 but drop ICMP, you'll see timeouts. Check cloud firewall for 'deny ICMP' rules.

raj-customer: Our security team denies all ICMP egress by policy. We opened a ticket but it's a tedious change. Any short-term workarounds?

jess-devex: Workarounds: 1) enable MSS clamping in the pod/node iptables so packets are smaller (iptables --table mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu on nodes), or 2) configure your firewall to allow ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation-needed), or 3) switch the agent pods to hostNetwork: true as a temporary measure (if acceptable) to avoid encapsulation.

mike-support: Also, because you have a default-deny NP, you need to explicitly allow egress to: DNS (UDP 53) and control-plane (TCP 443) and optionally health endpoints on 80/443. Example minimal egress rule:

---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-redwood-egress
  namespace: redwood
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.20.30.4/32 # control-plane
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector: {} # cluster dns svc if needed
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
---

raj-customer: We tried adding a NetworkPolicy allow for TCP/443 to control-plane IP and UDP/53 to kube-dns but still saw occasional failures until we fixed ICMP. After opening ICMP type3/4 in perimeter firewall and adding the MSS clamp on nodes, stability returned and agents re-registered.

redwood-agent-bot: [2026-03-14T09:58:12Z] registration successful for agent id arn:aws:ecs:...

mike-support: Good to hear. For long term: ask security to allow the ICMP fragmentation-needed message (type 3 code 4) at least to/from your control-plane IP range, or implement MSS clamping in your CNI/node bootstrap. Document the NP change in your change log.

jess-devex: Also make sure CA bundles are present on nodes/pods if you saw x509 errors earlier — we saw those during an earlier cert rotation in AWS when outgoing traffic was hitting a TLS-terminating proxy that rewrote certs.

raj-customer: Thanks all. Will open an internal ticket to whitelist control-plane IPs for the redwood service account, enable ICMP fragment-needed, and add the NP exception. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:

mike-support: Marking this thread resolved. If anything else pops up, ping us and we'll re-open. :white_check_mark:
